$comment: Neutral guardrail-hook SSOT for this repo — the hooks half of Argo's cross-CLI setup (skills are skills-lock.json's half). One entry per behavior; `packages/argo-skills/bin/hooks-sync.mjs` projects them into each harness named in `agents` below: claude-code -> .claude/settings.json, codex -> .codex/hooks.json. Never hand-edit those generated blocks — edit here and run `bun run hooks:sync`. Commands are harness-neutral: `$(git rev-parse --show-toplevel)/scripts/*` (no $CLAUDE_PROJECT_DIR). The commands invoke this repo's scripts/ via git-toplevel; scaffold.mjs can copy this file AND those scripts into a consumer before projecting, but only opt-in (`--hooks`) since the guard imposes Argo's worktree discipline. Optional top-level `worktreeGuard.roots` re-scopes the worktree edit guard (default `["apps", "packages"]`) for a project whose code lives elsewhere. See AGENTS.md "Cross-CLI guardrail hooks".

hooks.$comment: Creation-time naming guard. The edit guard above enforces THAT work runs in a worktree; this enforces WHICH — the branch and directory carry the ticket number, at the only moment the name is still free to change. It never fires on an edit inside an existing tree, so trees named before it drain untouched (#901).

The to-do-list nudge. AGENTS.md carries the same rule, but a rule that competes with a whole file for attention is one sessions skip: measured over 2981 transcripts, only 38% of sessions with three or more file edits wrote a list at all, and the rate fell over time (#1254). The script reads the session's own transcript and goes quiet the moment a list exists, and gives up after three prompts either way. It only ever adds context — it can never block a prompt.
